# UPPAbaby Aria V2 (1002-ARI, US)

- **Id:** `uppababy-aria-v2`
- **Category:** car-seat
- **Status:** shortlisted
- **Price:** $399.99
- **Brand:** UPPAbaby
- **Maker's page:** <https://uppababy.com/car-seats/infant/aria-v2/james/>
- **Decision:** none yet

## Summary

The lightest carrier on the shortlist, about 7 lb as used. Its base has a load leg and an anti-rebound panel, but its tightness indicator is unreliable, so always do the 1-inch movement test. Without the base it allows only European routing, so it cannot go on a lap-only or inflatable belt. No technician has reviewed the V2 by hand yet.

## Safety

- **Standards:** FMVSS 213, FMVSS 213a

- **Recalls:** none found in the search of 2026-11-28

## Pros

- Lightest carrier on the shortlist, about 7 lb as used (aria-v2 usability note).
- Baseless European-routing install was "super stable and firm" with no towel (BabyGearLab V2, aria-v2 usability note).
- Base has a load leg and an anti-rebound panel (market survey).
- Canopy rated "as close to perfect as an infant carrier can get" (BabyGearLab V2).
- No-rethread harness with 25 headrest positions (maker).

## Cons

Misuse risks come first.

- **Misuse risk:** the base's tightness indicator turned green before the base was tight, on V1 and on V2 (BabyGearLab); owners also report it falling back to red after driving (low confidence), as Mesa V3 owners do. CR (V1) lists the indicator as a pro, so the labs conflict. Always do the manual's 1-inch movement test.
- **Misuse risk:** on a vehicle-belt base install, the belt could slip in the lock-off when shaken (BabyGearLab V2). A Texas A&M KidSafe install demo got no movement with it, so V2 evidence conflicts. LATCH install avoids the question.
- **Misuse risk:** European routing is the only baseless method allowed; if a shoulder belt cannot reach around the shell, the V2 manual offers only customer service, no fallback. A car seat with a lap-only belt cannot take the carrier without its base (V1 allowed it).
- Inflatable vehicle seat belts are banned for every install, with or without the base (V2 manual p. 27).
- Outgrown by height sooner than most infant seats (30 in limit; CPST con on Babylist; V1 head-room data; V2 owner reports are mostly from an incentivized testing panel). Low confidence.
- Harness tightener has more resistance than most; hard to get snug without over-tightening (BabyGearLab V2).
- Stroller range is UPPAbaby strollers plus Mockingbird adapters (market survey).
- Not rated by NHTSA ease-of-use in the current feed (nhtsa ease-of-use note).
